title: IDD Journey Map
description: Schema for IDD journey map documents. Two step models are supported: the current array form (preferred) and the legacy keyed-object form. The 'non-sequential journey_step' rule and the assertion/action vocabularies are validator behaviors today; issues #38 and #39 replace them with kinded grammars and a declarative shape selector. Closed-world keys per #37.

description.description: Narrative summary of the journey this map describes.

preconditions.description: Narrative or structured preconditions that must hold for this journey-map to apply.

state_diagram.description: Optional embedded state diagram or reference to one. Free-form structure.

landing_decision_table.description: Decision table describing landing-page behavior. Free-form structure.

shape.description: Declarative journey-map shape (#39). Selects which step-ordering rule applies. Default is `sequential` for back-compat.

conformance.description: Conformance tier for the enclosing field. See SCHEMA.md.

branch.description: Used with shape:branching. Distinguishes steps that share a journey_step number by naming the branch the step belongs to.

action.description: A user or system action performed during a journey step. Either a legacy `type` (back-compat with the Playwright-vocab enum) or a kinded form (`kind` + attributes) must be present. The per-kind property vocabulary is author-extensible (target, url, value, timeout, until, variant, capture, …), so this object is intentionally open — typos won't be caught here.

type.description: Legacy action verb. Recognized values are navigate, click, fill, select, check, uncheck, wait, hover, scroll, press, type, upload. New documents are encouraged to use the expanded form.

kind.description: Broad category of action. ui-interaction covers DOM-level verbs; navigation covers route changes; wait covers delays or polling; network covers requests issued directly by the test; cli runs an installed command; install manages a package or executable; mcp calls a Model Context Protocol server; harness drives an agent-harness integration.

verb.description: Optional fine-grained verb when `kind` alone is too coarse (e.g., kind:ui-interaction, verb:double-click).

assertion.description: An expectation checked during a journey step. Either a legacy `type` (back-compat with the Playwright-vocab enum) or a kinded form (`kind` + property + target) must be present. The per-kind property vocabulary is author-extensible (selector, endpoint, expected, expected_status, contains, pattern, equals, fields, tag, min_seconds, …), so this object is intentionally open — typos won't be caught here.

type.description: Legacy assertion name. Recognized values are visible, hidden, text, url, api, count, polling, attribute, value, enabled, disabled. New documents are encouraged to use the expanded form.

kind.description: Broad category of assertion. dom / url / api / cookie are browser-shaped; classification / tag / context are domain-level; lifecycle asserts a modeled state; authority asserts a grant, scope, or principal continuity; content asserts required or forbidden content; package asserts installed-artifact state.

property.description: What about the kind is being asserted. For dom: visibility | text | value | attribute | enabled | count. For url: matches | contains | query. For cookie: set | present | max-age. Open string because each kind has its own property vocabulary.

target.description: What the assertion is about: a DOM selector, URL pattern, API endpoint, cookie name, classification name, tag name, or context key.

expected_status.description: Expected HTTP status code for kind:api assertions.

contains.description: Substring or fragment the assertion expects to find.

pattern.description: Regex or shape pattern the assertion expects to match.

name.description: Optional name for the assertion (useful when grouping).
